what: Confidence intervals and colors composition : variable_type × color × color_signif
title: Introduction to tabxplor
text: section reference behind two color sections . shows parameters fit together — variable type, measure color (color), significance policy (color_signif). type set column variable — factor (percentages computed, pct) numeric (means computed, mean). row variable always turned factor. Every colored table answers three questions: measure deviation? color = picks color means: "diff" (distance reference), "ratio" (relative risk percentages, mean ratio means), "contrib" (weight Chi-squared), "" (odds ratio). color = TRUE picks sensible one per column type. confident measure? every color reads one confidence interval conf_level (95% default). cell significant interval excludes neutral value — 0 difference, 1 ratio odds ratio. printed bracket, significance stars greying read interval, can never disagree. show significance? color_signif — "ignore", "grey_non_signif" "guaranteed_effect" ; stars = TRUE use significance stars instead , stacked , colors. confidence interval used colors stars compares cell reference cell (default, corresponding cell Total row Total column): Alternative interval methods (see ?tab_ci): - method_diff = "ac" (Agresti-Caffo) "wald" percentage difference; - method_mean_diff = "student" (pooled, OLS two-group interval) mean difference; - method_mean_ratio = "quasipoisson" "poisson" mean ratio. - relative-risk (method_ratio = "katz") odds-ratio (Woolf) intervals alternative. - mean difference colored standardized — Glass’s Δ, difference divided reference’s standard deviation — mean_diff color breaks read SD units, unless user provides custom break scale. - factor 3 levels, odds ratio (interval) compares level ref2 baseline level : relative risk ratio (RRR) (observed quantity modelised multinomial logistic regression). interval computed color_signif stars needs . Simple, cell--cell confidence intervals (ci = "cell") compare cell 0 % (mean 0), reference: compare 0 reference, cell intervals purely descriptive: carry significance stars. method_cell chooses "wilson" (default) "wald" percentages; mean cell interval always one-sample Student t. color_signif turns interval coloring policy. - "ignore" colors every cell observed effect size, example observed difference compared Total row. Grey cells observed effect threshold (example, differences less ±5 points percentages). - "grey_non_signif" "guaranteed_effect" color significant cells, differ intensity basis: + grey_non_signif colors observed effect, like “ignore”, greying small deviations, also greys large deviation turns non-significant. Ideal large samples. + guaranteed_effect colors guaranteed effect — confidence-bound (CI-floor), smaller deviation assured given confidence level (default 95%) — colors dimmer conservative, significative differences colored, ideal small samples. Examples :
code: # --- factors: percentages ------------------------------------------------- tab(gss_simple, race, party3, pct = "row", color = "diff",  color_signif = "grey_non_signif") tab(gss_simple, race, party3, pct = "row", color = "ratio", color_signif = "guaranteed_effect") tab(gss_simple, rincome, married, pct = "row", color = "OR", OR = TRUE, ref2 = 1) tab(gss_simple, rincome, party3, color = "contrib")   # works with pct = "row"/"col" too  # --- numerics: means ------------------------------------------------------ tab(gss_simple, rincome, tvhours, color = "diff",  color_signif = "guaranteed_effect") tab(gss_simple, rincome, tvhours, color = "ratio", color_signif = "grey_non_signif")  #    a custom scale for differences in means, and a "first row" reference tab(gss_simple, rincome, tvhours, color = "diff", color_signif = "grey_non_signif",     color_breaks = list(mean_diff = c(0.4, 0.8, 1.6)), ref = 1)

title: Introduction to tabxplor
text: handful options() set preferred defaults whole session — put top script, .Rprofile. one per-call argument ; option just changes default. everyday ones: options(tabxplor.print = "html") — print tables console, html RStudio Positron Viewer Pane default (recommended) options(tabxplor.cleannames = TRUE) — strip "1-"-style prefixes level names everywhere. options(tabxplor.parallel = 8) — parallelise tables multiples variables different CPU cores default (needs mirai) options(tabxplor.var_labels = TRUE) — exports, show variable’s label (haven/labelled data) instead bare name. options(tabxplor.theme = "auto") — export theme ("light"/"dark"/"auto"); set_color_palette(theme = "auto") console. options(tabxplor.stars = TRUE) — show significance stars every table (like stars = TRUE). options(tabxplor.conf_level = 0.9) — confidence level intervals tests (default 0.95). options(tabxplor.ci_print = "moe") — print confidence interval pct ± margin error instead [low; high] bracket. options(tabxplor.lang = "fr") — language colour legends footers ("auto"/"en"/"fr"). Colour thresholds palettes helpers, set_color_breaks() set_color_palette(). ?tabxplor-options documents every option, vignette("tabxplor-programming") covers advanced ones (export fonts, parallel builds…).

text: data analysis writing functions, can use sub-functions tab_many step step attain flexibility speed. way, ’s possible write new functions customize tables even . whole architecture tabxplor powered special vector class, named tabxplor_fmt formatted numbers. vctrs::record, stores behind scenes data necessary calculate printed results, formats colors. set functions available access transform data. ?fmt get information. simple way recover underlying numbers numeric vectors get_num, extract currently displayed field whatever : render character vectors (without colors), use format: following fields compose fmt column (though many can NA calculated) : display : name field display, customisable cell (character) n : raw count (integer) wn : weighted count pct : percentages diff : differences totals reference cells digits : digits display, customisable cell (integer) ctr : contributions cells variance (color = "contrib") mean : means (numeric column variables) var : variance (numeric column variables ; Chi2 variance pct) ci : confidence intervals rr : relative risks, needed calculate odds ratio : odds ratios (relative risks ratios) in_totrow : TRUE cell part total row, FALSE otherwise (logical) in_tottab : TRUE cell part total table, FALSE otherwise (logical) in_refrow : TRUE cell part reference row, FALSE otherwise (logical) get underlying fields can either use vctrs::fields , simply, $ : change field currently displayed, whole table single vector, can use set_display(): modify field, can use vctrs field<-. example, change number digits : Faster write easier read, can also use dplyr::mutate() fmt vector. example, create new column standards deviations display decimals : helper functions exists total rows, total tables reference rows (is_totrow() / as_totrow(), is_tottab() / as_tottab(), is_refrow() / as_refrow()) : fmt column attributes, can access modify get_ set_ functions : type / get_type() / set_type() : type fmt vector, among c("n", "mean", "row", "col", "", "all_tabs") ; determines calculations done within tab_ functions. totcol / is_totcol() / as_totcol() : TRUE column total column, FALSE otherwise (logical) refcol / is_refcol() / as_refcol() : TRUE column reference column comparison, FALSE otherwise (logical) color / get_color() / set_color() : calculation make print colors ; among c("", "", "diff", "diff_ci", "after_ci", "contrib") col_var / get_col_var() / set_col_var() : name column variable (can many one single table) comp_all / get_comp_all / set_comp_all() : tab_vars, reference comparison subtable (FALSE), total table (TRUE) ? ref / get_ref_type() / set_diff_type() : type difference calculated, either "", "tot" totals, index, regular expression. ci_type / get_ci_type() / set_ci_type() : type confidence interval, either "cell" "diff" example, print number observations total column : Note , tab_vars provided, table grouped operations made within groups. remove grouping (example gives errors), use dplyr::ungroup(). need simplest table, numeric counts (fmt), even base data.frame (tibble) :

A tabxplor tab: 4 × 9 #>   race   `No answer` `Never married` Separated Divorced Widowed Married Total #>   <fct>        <dbl>           <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 Other     0.00102            0.323    0.0562    0.108  0.0357   0.476     1 #> 2 Black     0.000639           0.417    0.0626    0.158  0.0837   0.278     1 #> 3 White     0.000793           0.212    0.0267    0.163  0.0900   0.507     1 #> 4 Total     0.000791           0.252    0.0346    0.157  0.0841   0.471     1 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: n <dbl> tabs |> mutate(across(where(is_fmt), format)) vctrs::vec_data(tabs$Married) #>       n display digits wn       pct      mean         diff ctr var ci rr or #> 1   932     pct      0 NA 0.4757529 1.0102402  0.004822432  NA  NA NA NA NA #> 2   869     pct      0 NA 0.2777245 0.5897357 -0.193205991  NA  NA NA NA NA #> 3  8316     pct      0 NA 0.5072278 1.0770757  0.036297310  NA  NA NA NA NA #> 4 10117     pct      0 NA 0.4709305 1.0000000  0.000000000  NA  NA NA NA NA #>   in_totrow in_tottab in_refrow #> 1     FALSE     FALSE     FALSE #> 2     FALSE     FALSE     FALSE #> 3     FALSE     FALSE     FALSE #> 4      TRUE     FALSE     FALSE tabs |> mutate(across(where(is_fmt), ~ vctrs::field(., "pct") ))  tabs$Married$pct tabs$Married$n tabs |> mutate(across(where(is_fmt), ~ .$n)) tabs |> set_display("diff") tabs |> mutate(across(where(is_fmt), ~ set_display(., "diff"))) tab(forcats::gss_cat, race, marital, pct = "row") |>      mutate(across(where(is_fmt), ~ vctrs::`field<-`(., "digits", rep(2L, length(.))))) tab_num(data, race, c(age, tvhours), marital, digits = 1L, comp = "all") |>   dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across( #Mutate over the whole table.     c(age, tvhours),     ~ dplyr::mutate(., #Mutate over each fmt vector's underlying data.frame.                     var     = sqrt(var),                      display = "var",                      digits  = 2L) |>        set_color("no"),     .names = "{.col}_sd"   )) tab(data, race, marital, year, pct = "row") |>   dplyr::mutate(across(      where(is_fmt),     ~ dplyr::if_else(is_totrow(.),                  true  = mutate(., digits = 1L),                  false = mutate(., digits = 2L))   )) tab(data, race, marital, year, pct = "row") |>   mutate(across(where(is_totcol), ~ mutate(., display = "n") )) tab_plain(data, race, marital, num = TRUE) # title: Print method for class tabxplor_fmt — format.tabxplor_fmt
text: x fmt object. ... parameters. html html tags added (print confidence intervals subscripts) ? na NAs printed. Default NA. special_formatting Set TRUE print verbose results, like indicating reference row col differences. stars Append significance stars value (opt-; default FALSE). Stars appear per-cell p-value stored (diff-type CIs / regression coefficients) right-padded numbers stay aligned. main display (console, tab_kable(), tab_md()) sets TRUE; tooltip / secondary-field re-renders leave FALSE, stars never leak. bold_split Internal (default FALSE): TRUE, attach per-cell primary_nchar attribute giving bold-prefix width composite "{pct} (n={n})" cell, exporters can bold primary field bold row. default -> output attribute-free. pad character used align numbers: pads values (composite displays, significance stars, confidence intervals, mean sd) separates thousands. Defaults plain space, figure space (U+2007, exactly one digit wide) html = TRUE. Media read monospace font (console, markdown) want plain space; media rendered proportional font (html, Excel) need figure space, since ASCII space half digit wide – CSS collapses runs . One glyph jobs, thousands mark can never disagree padding around . syntax "text" (default) returns rendered display strings; "excel" returns per-cell Excel number-format codes used tab_xl() (raw value written unchanged). .ref Internal: precomputed reference masks list(cells=, all_totals=) (derive-speed-passed exporter prep); computed internally NULL.

TRUE, adds descriptive crude (unadjusted, single-predictor) companion model effect factor-predictor level – unadjusted bivariate association, modelised quantity single predictor (standard "crude vs adjusted" comparison; large gap signals confounding). Per family: binomial adds Obs_% Obs_OR (coefficient) Obs_% + Obs_diff (AME); gaussian adds Obs_mean + Obs_diff; poisson adds Obs_rate + Obs_IRR; multinomial shows crude % + difference per category HTML tooltip (columns explode). design every crude quantity computed exactly complete-case population model (listwise-complete dependent, predictors design variable), crude adjusted directly comparable confounded differing missingness (reproduce dplyr::filter() + tab() rows). Also works vector dependents. Default FALSE. conf_level Confidence level intervals. Default 0.95. method interval p-value computed. "wald" (default) uses Wald interval Wald z / t test: fast, matches standard software output, option weighted models. "profile" uses profile-likelihood interval (stats::confint(), needs MASS) likelihood-ratio test: accurate near separation, unweighted binomial/poisson models (else falls back Wald message; gaussian always uses exact-t interval). stats goodness--fit statistics shown model-summary footer (one block per model). NULL (default) uses per-family set: linear models show N, R square, adjusted R square, overall F-test residual SD; models show N, likelihood-ratio test versus null model, McFadden's pseudo-R square, AIC BIC (poisson / grouped-binomial models also show Pearson dispersion). Defaults first model. estimate_display effect cell shows beside estimate. "prob"/"ame" need marginaleffects package apply binomial (logistic) coefficient models (degrade "ci" otherwise, message). title: Logistic-regression table (odds ratios) — tab_logit
text: data data frame, prebuilt survey design (survey::svydesign() / survey::svrepdesign()). design passed, weights (clustering / stratification / calibration) drive estimation wt / ids / strata / fpc ignored. dependent Character vector binary dependent variable name(s). must 2-level factor/character 0/1 numeric. predictors Character vector predictor variable name(s). wt Optional. Name weight column (character). Switches design-based survey estimation (survey::svyglm()): sandwich standard errors scale-invariant, raw population weights handled correctly (normalisation) point estimates match weighted crosstabs. ids, strata, fpc Optional survey-design specification wt path (column name / character vector, formula ~psu / ~region). ids gives cluster identifier(s) largest smallest stage (default clustering); strata stratifying variable(s); fpc finite-population correction. Give correct clustering/stratification honest design-based variances (flat ids = ~1 can understate ). Ignored data design. nest Logical. Passed survey::svydesign(): set TRUE cluster ids reused across strata. Default FALSE. inverse_two_level_factors Logical, binomial . TRUE (default), models FIRST level 2-level factor dependent (e.g. "1-Married" "2-married"). split_var Optional. Name grouping variable (character): regression analogue tab()'s tab_vars. model(s) fitted within level variable per-group tables stacked one grouped table (grouped split_var), sharing variable/level stub. Use tab_spread() split_var pivot groups side--side columns easy across-group comparison. level absent group shows empty cells. multiplier Optional named numeric vector c(var = k) rescaling continuous predictor's effect k-unit change (e.g. c(age = 10) shows odds ratio / beta per decade age = ^10 / beta*10). confidence interval scales ; p-value unchanged. Names must numeric predictors; available multinomial / ordinal outcomes. empirical Logical. TRUE, adds descriptive crude (unadjusted, single-predictor) companion model effect factor-predictor level – unadjusted bivariate association, modelised quantity single predictor (standard "crude vs adjusted" comparison; large gap signals confounding). Per family: binomial adds Obs_% Obs_OR (coefficient) Obs_% + Obs_diff (AME); gaussian adds Obs_mean + Obs_diff; poisson adds Obs_rate + Obs_IRR; multinomial shows crude % + difference per category HTML tooltip (columns explode). design every crude quantity computed exactly complete-case population model (listwise-complete dependent, predictors design variable), crude adjusted directly comparable confounded differing missingness (reproduce dplyr::filter() + tab() rows). Also works vector dependents. Ordinal clean crude analogue ignored (message). crude companion CIs descriptive, weighted data honour options(tabxplor.kish_neff = TRUE) (Kish's effective sample size) exactly like tab(); model column's CI always design-based (survey::svyglm) unaffected. Default FALSE. conf_level Confidence level intervals. Default 0.95. method interval p-value computed. "wald" (default) uses Wald interval Wald z / t test: fast, matches standard software output, option weighted models. "profile" uses profile-likelihood interval (stats::confint(), needs MASS) likelihood-ratio test: accurate near separation, unweighted binomial/poisson models (else falls back Wald message; gaussian always uses exact-t interval). stats goodness--fit statistics shown model-summary footer (one block per model). NULL (default) uses per-family set: linear models show N, R square, adjusted R square, overall F-test residual SD; models show N, likelihood-ratio test versus null model, McFadden's pseudo-R square, AIC BIC (poisson / grouped-binomial models also show Pearson dispersion). Pass character vector pick order statistics ("n", "lr_null", "mcfadden_r2", "aic", "bic", "dispersion", "r2", "r2_adj", "f_model", "sigma"), FALSE / "none" hide footer. Weighted models show reduced, survey-appropriate set (design-based Wald test, Nagelkerke pseudo-R square, AIC). estimate_display effect cell shows beside estimate. "value" (default) plain estimate (e.g. 2.34); "ci" adds visible confidence-interval bracket (2.34 [1.20; 4.50], family); "prob" folds model-adjusted predicted probability odds-ratio cell (2.34 (16%)); "ame" folds average marginal effect (2.34 (+8%)). "prob"/"ame" need marginaleffects package apply binomial (logistic) coefficient models (degrade "ci" otherwise, message). Note estimate_display = "ame" adds AME beside odds ratio, whereas effect = "ame" makes whole column AME (probability scale); two different , set, effect = "ame" wins estimate_display reset "value". color_signif significance drives colours. "grey_non_signif" (default) colours odds ratios whose confidence interval excludes 1 greys rest. stars Logical (default TRUE regression tables, significance stars standard). FALSE, per-cell p-value dropped stars shown (colours still read CI). na missing values handled across models. "drop_by_model" (default) drops NA rows per model (model / dependent uses complete cases). "drop_all_models" fits every model ONE shared complete-case population (rows NA predictor / dependent / design variable), nested models get equal N likelihood-ratio comparison can run; note changes estimates (shared population), hence opt-. Ignored prebuilt survey design. cleannames Logical. TRUE, strips numeric prefixes factor levels display. Uses getOption("tabxplor.cleannames") NULL. subtext Optional character. note shown table.

title: Means table — tab_num
text: data data frame. row_var row variable, printed one level per line. numeric, used factor. col_vars numeric variables, appear columns : means standard deviation calculated levels row_var tab_vars. tab_vars <tidy-select> Tab variables : subtable made combination levels selected variables. Leave empty make simple cross-table. tab variables converted factor. wt weight variable, class numeric. Leave empty unweighted results. color measure(s) color, channel – see tab full grammar (FALSE/TRUE, measure name, positional two-channel c("diff", "ratio") vector). numeric means useful measures "diff" (standardized, Glass's \(\Delta\)) "ratio" (mean ratio); TRUE uses "ratio". Default "auto" keeps historical behavior. color_signif significance gates color ("ignore" / "grey_non_signif" / "guaranteed_effect") – see tab. na policy adopt missing values row tab variables (factors), single string. "keep": default, NA's row tab variables printed explicit "NA" level. "drop": remove NA's row tab variables. NAs numeric variables always removed calculating means. reason n field resulting fmt column, used calculate confidence intervals, takes account complete observations (without NA). drop rows NA numeric variable first, use tab_prepare tab_many na_drop_all argument. ref reference cell calculate differences ratios (used print colors) : "auto": default, cell difference corresponding total (rows cols depending pct = "row" pct = "col") used diff ; cell ratio first line (col) use (odds ratio/relative risks ratio). "tot": totals always used. "first": calculate cell difference ratio first cell row column (useful color temporal developments). n: ref integer, nth row (column) used comparison. Leave NULL dependent formula. split_var Optional. Name grouping variable (character): regression analogue tab()'s tab_vars. model(s) fitted within level variable per-group tables stacked one grouped table (grouped split_var), sharing variable/level stub. Use tab_spread() split_var pivot groups side--side columns easy across-group comparison. level absent group shows empty cells. wt Optional. Name weight column (character). Switches design-based survey estimation (survey::svyglm()): sandwich standard errors scale-invariant, raw population weights handled correctly (normalisation) point estimates match weighted crosstabs. family model family, resolved per dependent several outcomes different families can share one table (one effect column-group ). "auto" (default) detects outcome: binary (-> "binomial"), ordered 3+ level (-> "ordinal"), nominal 3+ level (-> "multinomial"), continuous (-> "gaussian") outcome, emitting message; integer count stays ambiguous must named (outcome ). Set explicitly "gaussian" (linear), "binomial" (logistic), "poisson" / "quasipoisson" (counts), "multinomial" (nominal 3+ level), "ordinal" (ordered 3+ level). scalar applies every dependent; vector aligned dependent, named vector keyed dependent (e.g. c(income = "poisson", satisfied = "binomial")), sets one family per outcome. Mixed families work character predictors (one model per outcome); predictors list (model comparison) single-outcome, hence single-family. -dispersed counts. unweighted "poisson" fit auto-scales standard errors square root Pearson dispersion, -dispersed outcome (dispersion clearly 1) CIs p-values identical "quasipoisson", warns say (footer reports dispersion). equidispersion (\(\approx\)1) scaling -op result matches standard glm(family = poisson) z-interval — user comparing hand-fit Poisson glm surprised wider intervals. effect interpretation scale, orthogonal family. "coefficient" (default) shows native per-family effect (beta / / IRR / cumulative-). "ame" shows average marginal effects adjusted predicted probability parentheses (e.g. -8%*** (16%)): probability-scale, cross-model-comparable summary (Mood 2010) logistic / multinomial / ordinal outcomes (percentage points), expected-count change poisson, coefficient gaussian. parenthetical marginal-standardized prediction (avg_predictions(variables=): predictor set level whole sample, covariates kept observed, averaged), genuinely covariate-adjusted coheres effect — adjusted-%(reference) AME(level) equals adjusted-%(level). Read standardized comparison ("holding measured covariates' distribution fixed"), manipulation. Requires marginaleffects package. multinomial / ordinal outcome gets one AME column per outcome category. profile-conditional quantities evaluated (needs marginaleffects). "average" (default) sample average (AME / adjusted prediction data). "reference" evaluates reference profile — every predictor held reference (factor first level, numeric mean): effect = "ame" gives marginal effect reference (MER) adjusted prediction ; multinomial effect = "coefficient" gives odds ratio outcome category versus rest profile (one column per category). effect ordinary coefficients (profile-independent). Note reference profile can unusual baseline (e.g. factor's first level = "answer"). exponentiate Logical. TRUE (default) exponentiates coefficients ratios (odds ratios logistic, incidence-rate ratios poisson, cumulative odds ratios ordinal), automatically leaving gaussian linear betas raw scale. FALSE keeps every coefficient coefficient (log / linear) scale. Ignored effect = "ame" (marginal effects always response scale). trials Grouped-binomial (summed-score) outcomes . number items behind score, fitting cbind(score, trials - score) binomial. NULL (default) fits ordinary binary logit; single integer (vector named dependent) sets item count; TRUE uses dependent's observed maximum score. Requires family = "binomial". empirical Logical. TRUE, adds descriptive crude (unadjusted, single-predictor) companion model effect factor-predictor level – unadjusted bivariate association, modelised quantity single predictor (standard "crude vs adjusted" comparison; large gap signals confounding). Per family: binomial adds Obs_% Obs_OR (coefficient) Obs_% + Obs_diff (AME); gaussian adds Obs_mean + Obs_diff; poisson adds Obs_rate + Obs_IRR; multinomial shows crude % + difference per category HTML tooltip (columns explode). design every crude quantity computed exactly complete-case population model (listwise-complete dependent, predictors design variable), crude adjusted directly comparable confounded differing missingness (reproduce dplyr::filter() + tab() rows). Also works vector dependents. Ordinal clean crude analogue ignored (message). crude companion CIs descriptive, weighted data honour options(tabxplor.kish_neff = TRUE) (Kish's effective sample size) exactly like tab(); model column's CI always design-based (survey::svyglm) unaffected. Default FALSE. color, color_signif Colouring effect cells. color = TRUE (default) auto-picks sensible per-family measure ("" magnitude ratios, standardized "diff" betas); color = FALSE turns colouring every column (model empirical). Power users may pass measure string ("", "diff", "ratio", "") override. color_signif significance policy (default "grey_non_signif"). See tab(). stars Logical (default TRUE regression tables, significance stars standard). FALSE, per-cell p-value dropped stars shown (colours still read CI). conf_level Confidence level intervals. Default 0.95. method interval p-value computed. "wald" (default) uses Wald interval Wald z / t test: fast, matches standard software output, option weighted models. "profile" uses profile-likelihood interval (stats::confint(), needs MASS) likelihood-ratio test: accurate near separation, unweighted binomial/poisson models (else falls back Wald message; gaussian always uses exact-t interval). reference Optional named vector c(var = "baseline level") choosing treatment-contrast reference level one factor predictors (effect every level measured ). multinomial outcome, keying vector outcome name (e.g. c(partyid = "Independent")) also sets baseline outcome category columns compared . factor contrasts set; contrast codings can applied passing formula dependent terms already coded. inverse_two_level_factors Logical, binomial . TRUE (default), models FIRST level 2-level factor dependent (e.g. "1-Married" "2-married"). multiplier Optional named numeric vector c(var = k) rescaling continuous predictor's effect k-unit change (e.g. c(age = 10) shows odds ratio / beta per decade age = ^10 / beta*10). confidence interval scales ; p-value unchanged. Names must numeric predictors; available multinomial / ordinal outcomes. stats goodness--fit statistics shown model-summary footer (one block per model). NULL (default) uses per-family set: linear models show N, R square, adjusted R square, overall F-test residual SD; models show N, likelihood-ratio test versus null model, McFadden's pseudo-R square, AIC BIC (poisson / grouped-binomial models also show Pearson dispersion). Pass character vector pick order statistics ("n", "lr_null", "mcfadden_r2", "aic", "bic", "dispersion", "r2", "r2_adj", "f_model", "sigma"), FALSE / "none" hide footer. Weighted models show reduced, survey-appropriate set (design-based Wald test, Nagelkerke pseudo-R square, AIC). compare Add model-comparison footer row (several models / dependents). "none" (default) adds nothing; "baseline" tests model baseline column; "sequential" tests model previous one. Uses likelihood-ratio test (F linear / quasi models, design-based Wald test weighted / survey models); models nested fit different numbers observations falls back AIC difference message. baseline compare = "baseline": column reference model (label, position). Defaults first model. na missing values handled across models. "drop_by_model" (default) drops NA rows per model (model / dependent uses complete cases). "drop_all_models" fits every model ONE shared complete-case population (rows NA predictor / dependent / design variable), nested models get equal N likelihood-ratio comparison can run; note changes estimates (shared population), hence opt-. Ignored prebuilt survey design. estimate_display effect cell shows beside estimate. "value" (default) plain estimate (e.g. 2.34); "ci" adds visible confidence-interval bracket (2.34 [1.20; 4.50], family); "prob" folds model-adjusted predicted probability odds-ratio cell (2.34 (16%)); "ame" folds average marginal effect (2.34 (+8%)). "prob"/"ame" need marginaleffects package apply binomial (logistic) coefficient models (degrade "ci" otherwise, message). Note estimate_display = "ame" adds AME beside odds ratio, whereas effect = "ame" makes whole column AME (probability scale); two different , set, effect = "ame" wins estimate_display reset "value". cleannames Logical. title: Regression table (effect measures) as a tabxplor table — tab_reg
text: New regressions tabxplor? first model needs three arguments: data, dependent (outcome) predictors. tabxplor picks right model outcome's type — two-level factor gives logistic odds ratios, numeric gives linear betas, count gives Poisson rate ratios, 3+ level factor gives multinomial ordinal odds ratios — rarely set family hand. Add empirical = TRUE show crude (unadjusted) effect beside model's adjusted one. See vignette("tabxplor-reg") guided tour. arguments fall groups: model: data, dependent, predictors (character vector = one model; named list = several models compare), family (usually detected), wt (survey weights). cell shows: exponentiate, effect ("coefficient" average marginal effect "ame"), estimate_display, empirical (crude vs adjusted effect). Colors & significance: color, color_signif, stars, conf_level — tab(). Comparisons & structure: reference (baseline levels), compare / baseline (model comparison test), split_var (one table per group), multiplier (effect per k units). Survey design: wt, ids, strata, fpc, nest, pass prebuilt design data. Diagnostics: stats (footer statistics), plots or_plot() / lm_plots(). predictors selects mode: character vector fits one model, dependent may vector -> one column per dependent; named list predictor sets fits one model -> one column per model (predictors absent model left blank), comparing specifications. effect = "ame" switches native coefficient average marginal effects adjusted predicted probability shown parentheses (e.g. -8%*** (16%)) – probability-scale, cross-model-comparable interpretation (Mood 2010), computed marginaleffects package. = "reference" instead evaluates reference profile (predictors held reference level / mean): marginal effect reference, – multinomial effect = "coefficient" – odds ratio outcome category versus rest profile. Unweighted models use stats::lm() / stats::glm(); wt weight column switches survey design (survey::svyglm()), gives correct design-based standard errors rather frequency-inflated ones glm(weights=). broom (always) survey (wt) optional dependencies. tab_logit() / multi_logit() convenience wrappers binomial family. nominal outcome 3+ unordered levels fit one multinomial logit (nnet::multinom()), giving one odds-ratio column per non-reference outcome category ("<category> vs <reference>: "). ordered outcome 3+ levels fit proportional-odds cumulative logit (MASS::polr()), giving one cumulative-odds-ratio column; parallel-lines assumption tested Brant test (install brant package) warning issued violated. (Weighted 3+ level models planned later release.) summed-score outcome (count "yes" answers fixed number items) fit grouped binomial pass trials (number items). Power users can pass model formula dependent – tab_reg(data, y ~ x1 + poly(x2, 2) + x1:x3) – driving model directly; simple y ~ + b formulas behave exactly like dependent = "y", predictors = c("", "b"), interactions / poly() / () terms render best-effort term rows.

title: tabxplor global options — tabxplor-options
text: tabxplor.print "console" (default) "kable": table auto-prints. tabxplor.stars FALSE (default): whether cells show significance stars (*/**/***). tab(), tab_reg(). Per-call stars =. tabxplor.signif_levels p-value cut-offs stars, default c(0.10, 0.05, 0.01). tabxplor.signif_labels star labels, default c("*", "**", "***"). tabxplor.ci_print "ci" (default) shows [inf; sup] interval; "moe" shows larger half-width (margin error). tabxplor.totcol_range Total column's -cell base shown table's column variables differing bases (e.g. na = "drop"): "" (default) row's base; "range" per-row [min;max]; "min" smallest (safest) base. tabxplor.var_names variable names exporters annotate: "" (default), "rows", "cols", "none". Per-call var_names =. tabxplor.var_labels FALSE (default): exports (markdown / html / Excel / plot), show variable's label (haven/labelled label attribute, one) instead name. Display – table structure keeps canonical names, name-based select() references still work; console always shows names. tabxplor.cleannames FALSE (default): clean variable/level names output. Also strips "1-"-style prefix labelled value labels turned factor levels.

title: tabxplor global options — tabxplor-options

Auto-detected load: TRUE Positron VS Code (render ANSI bold fixed glyph width), FALSE RStudio unknown consoles (bold drawn wider break column alignment). title: tabxplor global options — tabxplor-options
text: tabxplor.anova one-way ANOVA F shown mean columns: "welch" (default, robust) "classic" (pooled variance). always stored test attribute. tabxplor.test_lines many crosstab test rows exporters (tab_md(), tab_html(), tab_xl()) append: "summary" (default: p-value + effect size), "" (+ raw statistic), "stat" (p-value + statistic), "pvalue" (single p-value row). p-value row name states test used ("pvalue (Chi2, Welch F; Kish)") effect-size row name measure ("Cramer's V, eta2"). N never added – already shown add_n. console summary block always shows N + p-value + effect size. tabxplor.legend_style colour-legend style exports (tab_md(), tab_kable(), tab_xl(), tab_plot()): "prose" (default, full sentences) "terse" (compact one-line form console uses). console always terse. tabxplor.kish_neff FALSE default (weighted estimate, raw unweighted n). Set TRUE replace raw n Kish's effective sample size n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) every weighted descriptive confidence interval – factor proportions means (cell, difference, ratio color = "" significance) tab() / tab_num() / tab_counts(), crude empirical = companions tab_reg(). unequal weights n_eff < n, intervals widen honestly (otherwise carry design effect run narrow). also switches whole-table tests (test = TRUE) first-order Rao-Scott correction – factor chi-square rescaled n_eff, numeric F per-group n_eff. single-stage unequal-weight approximation, design-based analysis: needs microdata weights, tab_counts() pre-aggregated counts apply . regression model CIs tab_reg() already fully design-based (survey::svyglm) unaffected. full design-based whole-table test (clusters / strata) use test = "survey" wt =/strata =/ids =, pass survey::svydesign data. tabxplor.conf_level confidence level intervals significance tests, default 0.95. per-call conf_level = argument tab(), tab_num(), tab_ci() tab_reg() overrides .

title: tabxplor 1.4.0
text: tab() now unified entry point. accepts several row_vars / col_vars (e.g. tab(data, c(race, relig), marital)), merged one table default returned list output_list = TRUE. tab_many() kept soft-deprecated alias. Redesigned colour API. Position picks visual channel (1st value → text, 2nd → background), names pick column type (pct / mean); color = TRUE smart per-type default. New OKLCH light/dark palettes, 24-bit truecolor console, set_color_palette() (replaces set_color_style()), per-table color_breaks = argument. Dark mode. theme = "auto" tab_html() / tab_md() / tab_css() / tab_export() follows whoever reading table (browser, editor Viewer). console also auto-detects dark editor (RStudio Positron). new, dependency-free HTML engine, now default tab_html() (3× faster much lighter kableExtra, becomes optional). geometry CSS classes, CSS can restyle . Significance stars correct confidence intervals. Stars opt-(stars =); cell / difference / mean intervals now proper asymmetric intervals (Wilson, Newcombe, Welch) stars read interval. ci gains "ratio"; method_cell / method_diff / method_mean_diff / method_mean_ratio / method_ratio choose interval. Mean columns get whole-table test — one-way ANOVA (Welch classic, options(tabxplor.anova)), counterpart chi-squared factor columns. Effect sizes, Fisher’s exact survey-robust p-values. test = TRUE now carries Cramér’s V / phi eta²; small sparse table uses Fisher’s exact; test = "survey" (ids / strata / fpc / nest, survey::svydesign data) options(tabxplor.kish_neff = TRUE) give design-based / effective-sample-size p-values confidence intervals. Readable colour legends footers, fully translatable French (options(tabxplor.lang = "fr"), lang = argument, R/OS locale). Labelled-data (haven) support. Value labels become factor levels; options(tabxplor.var_labels = TRUE) shows variable labels instead names exports. New arguments tab(): na gains "common_base" /, spread_vars =, n_min = (hide small-base cells), display = (composite cells like "{pct} (n={n})"), common_totrow =, per-col_var / positional ref, parallel = (opt-, needs mirai). tab_counts() — build full colour-coded table already-aggregated counts (long, wide, table, frequencies + base N) instead microdata. tab_reg() — colour-coded regression tables (linear / logistic / Poisson / multinomial / ordinal), survey weights, model comparison, average marginal effects, Excel / HTML / Markdown export. See regression vignette. tab_logit() / multi_logit() thin wrappers; or_plot() / lm_plots() draw . tab_export() — one entry point every export format. tab_html() new name tab_kable() (kept permanent alias). tab_css() generates one stylesheet whole document. set_caption() / get_caption() store caption survives pipeline. tab_transpose() / transpose = TRUE — flip table, mainly column-percentage inversion workflow. Also: French vignettes bilingual pkgdown website. New jamovi “Regression models” analysis (jmvtabreg) tab_reg(). Crosstables module (jmvtab) gains reference-level picker, export, live cache, new options.

what: Changes that may affect existing code
title: tabxplor 1.4.0
text: Excel export now uses openxlsx2 (Suggests) instead openxlsx. Dependencies reshuffled. magrittr / stringr / crayon dropped, %>% longer re-exported — use base |> pipe (load magrittr/dplyr). kableExtra DescTools move Suggests; survey / nnet / MASS / broom become hard dependencies (weighted, multinomial, ordinal basic tab_reg() work box). Significance stars opt-(default) tab(); tab_reg() still shows . add_n, add_pct chi-squared / ANOVA p-values now drawn display/export time, stored columns/rows built object. Read via get_n() Total column test attribute (get_test()). numeric (mean) columns, diff field now real difference; cell/reference ratio moved ratio field. tab(na = "drop") several col_vars now drops column’s missing values (old shared base now na = "drop_all"). options got clearer names (tabxplor.kable_css → tabxplor.tab_kable_css, plus tabxplor.console_theme / tabxplor.export_theme); old names still work.

title: tabxplor 1.4.0
text: factor carrying NA real level (factor(..., exclude = NULL), common imported data) longer crashes print() / format() / export. tab() accepts data.table input, logical col_var. Clearer errors unknown named ref, variable used tab row/column variable, -zero / -NA weight. lang argument now works Linux (lang = "fr" used return English legend).

title: tabxplor 1.4.0
text: Soft-deprecated (still work): tab_many() (use tab() several row_vars / col_vars); singular row_var / col_var; tab(sup_cols =) (use col_vars =); tab(filter =) (filter upstream). tab_pct() / tab_tot() / tab_totaltab(); tab_transpose() (use transpose = TRUE); tab_plot(). Renamed arguments: chi2 → test, tab_xl(print_color_legend =) →color_legend =. combined colour strings "diff_ci" / "after_ci" / "ci" (use color = "diff" + color_signif =); color_type (now inert). Removed / defunct (now error): tab_xl(n_min =, hide_near_zero =) (long inert); little-used totcol vector forms; tabxplor.compact option (use output_list =).
